catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexander-v: This 1913 reference piece on Alexander V — the Pisan pope of the great schism. John Bertram Peterson explains his tragic election. Pisa's council meant to heal the split. It only made three popes. A good man in an impossible chair. His tomb lies in Bologna's church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-boniface-v: This 1913 reference piece on Boniface V — the pope of the Northumbrian mission. Thomas Oestereich honors his letters. He cheered Edwin's conversion. The entry preserves his modest fame. A pope of the seventh century. His letters reached the English kings.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-emperor-charl: This 1913 reference article on Charles V — the emperor of the vast dominion. Martin Spahn unfolds his world-wide reign. His fleets spanned the Atlantic's main. Yuste saw the abdicated monarch. The master of the sixteenth-century world. His 1558 death is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-felix-v: This 1913 reference article on Felix V — the Savoyard antipope. Johann Peter Kirsch unfolds his Basel election. He wore the triple crown in vain. The Church kept the Roman line. The last of the Western antipopes. His 1449 abdication is famed.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-henry-v: This 1913 reference article on Henry V — the Salian emperor. Franz Kampers unfolds his mighty reign. He humbled the papal throne. The empire knew the fearless lord. The master of the twelfth-century Reich. His 1125 death is famed.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DollahiteVernon:
Patrolman Vernon V. Dollahite of Shelby County was interviewed by the FBI on April 13, 1968. Memphis police and Special Agent Franklin L. Johnson took part. Nine days earlier, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. had been shot at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, and officers across the area were accounting for their movements.

Dollahite re-enacted what he had done on April 4, the day of the shooting. Interviews of this kind built the investigation's timeline, placing each officer at each hour. His statement preserves one patrolman's part in that record, fixed while memories were still fresh.
al-masudi-prairies-dor-meynard-vol-v:
The fifth tome of Barbier de Meynard's Les Prairies d'Or appeared in 1869, midway in the nine-tome French set. Its author, al-Masudi of Baghdad, finished the Muruj al-Dhahab, the Meadows of Gold and Mines of Gems, in the last years of his life. He had spent decades on the roads and seas of Asia and Africa.

Few medieval books hold so much. The science of the earth, the tales of ancient kings, and the ways of Hindus, Persians, and Franks all stand beside the chronicle of the caliphs. Al-Masudi wrote to teach and to delight at once. The French editors add notes on the hard names and places. This middle tome carries the reader deep into the whole.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-adrian-v: Adrian V was the pope whose reign lasted a single month in 1276. This entry traces his election, his brief days, and his death. The pope of thirty-nine days: his strange death gave Dante a famous papal cameo in Purgatory.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-benedict: Benedict V was the pope the Romans chose and the emperor deposed. This entry traces his brief pontificate, his exile, and his death at Hamburg. The pope of a single month: his unjust deposition pleased the conquering emperor Otto the Great.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-bl-urban: Urban V was the blessed pope who brought the papacy back to Rome from Avignon. This entry traces his pontificate, his return, and his sanctity. The reformer of the Avignon age: his brief return thrilled the faithful Romans of 1367.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-celestin: Celestine V was the hermit pope who resigned the tiara. This entry traces his election, his abdication, and Dante's judgment. The saint who made the great refusal: his hermit cell became his stolen throne's dark and lonely shadow forevermore in defeat.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-clement-: Clement V was the pope who moved to Avignon and dissolved the Templars. This entry traces his pontificate, his trials, and his infamy. The pope of the Babylonian captivity: his fateful move doomed the poor Templars to the fiery stake.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-gregory-: Gregory V was the first German pope, Otto III's young kinsman. This entry traces his pontificate, his youth, and his sudden death. The Saxon on Peter's throne: his tender youth served the boy emperor faithfully and well in imperial Rome.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-innocent: Innocent V was the Dominican pope whose five months ended the long vacancy. This entry traces his brief pontificate, his learning, and his death. The friar of the short spring: his deep learning graced the papal throne briefly but brightly.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-john-v: John V was the Syrian pope of 686, first elected without imperial confirmation. This entry notes his brief pontificate and his precedent. The pope of the free election: his free choice needed no emperor's leave in distant Byzantium anymore at all.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-leo-v: Leo V was the pope deposed and murdered in 903. This entry notes his brief pontificate, his fall, and the scant records. A victim of the dark century's violence: his brutal successor strangled him in prison at dark and violent Rome.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-martin-v: Martin V was the pope of Constance who ended the Great Schism. This entry traces his pontificate, his election, and his restoration of Rome. The restorer of the papacy: his ruined Rome rose from the ashes of the long schism.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-nicholas: Nicholas V was the humanist pope who founded the Vatican Library. This entry traces his pontificate, his scholars, and his Rome. The pope of the Renaissance dawn: his great library seeded the Vatican's own great collection of books and manuscripts.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-paul-v: Paul V was the Borghese pope of the Venetian interdict and Galileo's first trial. This entry traces his pontificate, his fountains, and his sternness. The pope of the Acqua Paola: his mighty fountain waters Rome still today in baroque splendor.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-sixtus-v: Sixtus V was the iron Peretti pope who remade Rome in five years. This long entry traces his pontificate, his obelisks, and his reforms. The greatest administrator of the age: his soaring dome crowns St. Peter's today in eternal glory.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-st-pius-: Pius V was the saintly Dominican pope of Lepanto and the Tridentine Mass. This long entry traces his pontificate, his rosary crusade, and his sanctity. The pope of the great victory: his blessed rosary won Lepanto's glorious day in 1571.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-stephen-: Stephen IV was the pope who crowned Louis the Pious at Reims. This entry notes his brief pontificate, his journey, and the scant records. The pope of the imperial unction: his sacred crown blessed the waiting emperor at Reims in 816.
king-henry-v: Shakespeare's heroic history play: young Henry V unites England, invades France, and wins the miracle victory of Agincourt. "Once more unto the breach" and the St. Crispin's Day speech made it the classic celebration of leadership. Stirring, patriotic, and more thoughtful about war than it first appears.
un-doc-united-nations-special-committee-:
Chapter V of the 1947 report of the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine weighs what could be done about the land's future. UNSCOP had toured Palestine and heard Jews and Arabs state rival claims. Britain was ending its mandate, and a choice could not be put off.

The chapter tests the main options against the facts the panel had gathered. It looks at partition, a single shared state, and other plans for rule. It sets out the gains and costs of each path. This groundwork leads straight to the rival plans that close the report.

20762-chancellorsville-and-gettysburg-ca:
Abner Doubleday fought at Gettysburg, and his campaign history speaks with a soldier's frankness. He warns that fresh events draw sharp fire from those who lived them. A bland tale that praises all and blames none, he says, would waste the war's hard lessons.

Chancellorsville and Gettysburg, two vast battles of 1863, fill this volume of the Campaigns of the Civil War set. Doubleday held ground at Gettysburg on the first day. His account weighs plans, ground, and command choices in plain terms. Readers get a Union view from a man who stood in the line himself.
